[Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump"), the 45th and 47th [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States"), was born on June 14, 1946, in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") to [Fred Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Trump "Fred Trump"), a real-estate developer, and [Mary Anne MacLeod Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Anne_MacLeod_Trump "Mary Anne MacLeod Trump"). He was raised in a strict household and developed a rebellious and braggadocious personality early in his youth.
Trump enrolled at the [Kew-Forest School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kew-Forest_School "Kew-Forest School"), a private school affiliated with Fred, when he was five. He developed an aptitude for a variety of sports, particularly baseball. In his seventh-grade year, Fred discovered that Trump had secretly been going to [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"), where he acquired knives. Fred sent Trump to [New York Military Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Military_Academy "New York Military Academy") from which he graduated in May 1964.
After graduating from the academy, he attended [Fordham University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fordham_University "Fordham University") from 1964 to 1966, studying economics. His college enrollment—and later a medical exemption—allowed him to defer the [Vietnam War draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War_draft "Vietnam War draft"). Early in his [sophomore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophomore "Sophomore") year, seeking a larger [business network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_network "Business network"), Trump transferred to the [Wharton School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wharton_School "Wharton School") at the [University of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania "University of Pennsylvania"), an institution favored by his father. He did not participate in extracurricular activities after his [freshman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freshman "Freshman") year. Trump graduated from the University of Pennsylvania in May 1968 with a [Bachelor of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") in economics.

to cause mischief regardless of consequence.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201734-38) He later contended that he gave his music teacher a black eye in second grade,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHurt199376-39) believing that, in his telling, the teacher was clueless about music.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTED'Antonio201540-37)[[g]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-40) In interviews conducted for _[Trump Revealed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump_Revealed "Trump Revealed")_ (2017), a close friend of Trump, [Peter Brant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Brant "Peter Brant"), could not recall the incident occurring or Trump mentioning that it had happened.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201735-41) Detentions at Kew-Forest became known as "Donny Trumps" for Trump's notorious behavior.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201734-38) In contrast, some former classmates who spoke to [Maggie Haberman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maggie_Haberman "Maggie Haberman") for her book _[Confidence Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confidence_Man:_The_Making_of_Donald_Trump_and_the_Breaking_of_America "Confidence Man: The Making of Donald Trump and the Breaking of America")_ described Trump as "sweet and fun to be around".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHaberman202225-42)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Kew-Forest_School%27s_6th_Grade_Class_%281958%29.jpg/250px-Kew-Forest_School%27s_6th_Grade_Class_%281958%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kew-Forest_School's_6th_Grade_Class_\(1958\).jpg)The Kew-Forest School sixth grade class in 1958 with Trump (back row, fourth from the right)
To discourage Trump from causing further mischief, his mother, a devout Christian, sent Trump to confirmation classes at [First Presbyterian Church in Jamaica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Presbyterian_Church_in_Jamaica "First Presbyterian Church in Jamaica").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHurt199376%E2%80%9377-43) Trump's behavior remained consistent at Sunday school and home, where he occasionally rebuffed his father.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTED'Antonio201540-37) In fourth grade, he was the tallest in his class of sixteen, giving him an advantage in sports.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202461-36) Though Trump's grades suffered, he was adept at a variety of sports, including punchball, basketball, football, and soccer. Trump was particularly passionate about baseball, playing the position of [catcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catcher "Catcher"), and admired the catchers [Yogi Berra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yogi_Berra "Yogi Berra") of the [New York Yankees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Yankees "New York Yankees") and [Roy Campanella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Campanella "Roy Campanella") of the [Brooklyn Dodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Dodgers "Brooklyn Dodgers"). On several occasions, he secretly brought a transistor radio into class and listened to baseball with earplugs.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201735%E2%80%9336-44) Trump had a [paper route](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paperboy "Paperboy") and rounded up bottles for deposits. With Brant, he would take the [New York City Subway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Subway "New York City Subway") to [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan") to purchase gag gifts—such as [smoke bombs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoke_bombs "Smoke bombs"), and later [switchblades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switchblades "Switchblades")—to play a game that involved throwing knives at a target.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlair2000232%E2%80%93233-45) Their fascination with the blades developed after the premiere of _[West Side Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Side_Story "West Side Story")_ , a musical featuring street fighting,[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202463-46) in 1957, when they were eleven.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlair2000233-47)
## Military school
[![Young Trump at bat](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Donald_Trump_playing_baseball_%28cropped%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Donald_Trump_playing_baseball_%28cropped%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Donald_Trump_playing_baseball_\(cropped\)_\(cropped\).jpg)Trump playing baseball in 1962 (NYMA yearbook photo)
Near the end of Trump's seventh-grade year, his father, Fred, discovered his cache of knives and learned of his adventures in Manhattan.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlair2000233-47) The revelations infuriated Fred, who decided to send Trump to [New York Military Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Military_Academy "New York Military Academy")[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlair2000233-47) (NYMA) in [Cornwall-on-Hudson, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornwall-on-Hudson,_New_York "Cornwall-on-Hudson, New York").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201738-48) Prior to attending the academy, Trump went to Camp Hilltop, an expensive, Christian, carefully-supervised outdoor camp in [Hancock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hancock,_New_York "Hancock, New York"), as his brother, [Freddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Trump_Jr. "Fred Trump Jr."), had done years earlier—an experience that made him ornery and bored.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlair2000234%E2%80%93235-49) He arrived at NYMA in September 1959, and was advised by Theodore Dobias, a [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") veteran.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201738%E2%80%9339-50) Dobias struck insubordinate cadets and conducted cage matches between disobedient students twice a week.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201739-51) Trump was [physically abused](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_abuse "Physical abuse") with slaps and blows.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHaberman202226-52) Older cadets often used violence, or threats of violence, to assume authority.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202465-53) According to Dobias, Trump was reluctant to conform to the expectations of the academy, but he quickly excelled at hygiene requirements, sought to compete for contests in order and cleanliness, and worked for higher grades.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201739%E2%80%9340-54) Trump later described his tenure as contingent on "survival".[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTED'Antonio201545-55) In interviews, former cadets told [Gwenda Blair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwenda_Blair "Gwenda Blair") for _[The Trumps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Trumps:_Three_Generations_That_Built_an_Empire "The Trumps: Three Generations That Built an Empire")_ (2000) that Trump was socially distant with everyone except for Dobias.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlair2000237-56) Trump returned to [Jamaica Estates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamaica_Estates "Jamaica Estates") each summer to help his father with apartment maintenance.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202466-57)
[![Five students shown full length in uniform](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/1964_NYMA_-_5_students_in_uniform.jpg/250px-1964_NYMA_-_5_students_in_uniform.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1964_NYMA_-_5_students_in_uniform.jpg)Trump (second from left) in 1964
Trump played sports at NYMA—one year each of varsity football and soccer, and three years of varsity baseball[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202466-57) as a cleanup hitter and, during his senior year, as a [first baseman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_baseman "First baseman").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBarrett201673-58) Dobias coached Trump in his time on the junior varsity baseball team,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202466-57) and he was informally named as an assistant coach[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlair2000238-59) and a co-captain in his senior year.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202466-57) Trump had a poor batting average of .056 in his final year, according to box scores.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202466-57) His later boasts notwithstanding, Trump was neither the best baseball player in New York, nor the academy's best athlete.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202471-60) Dobias later told Blair that Trump was "aggressive but so coachable"; in Trump's telling, he "finessed" Dobias by respecting him without becoming overcome with fear.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlair2000238-59) Trump's decision to quit the football team his junior year, citing an apparently abusive coach,[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201742-61) drew criticism from some other students.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHurt199378-62) When a local newspaper headline said he helped to win a baseball game, Trump was amazed at seeing his name in print and marveled at his fame.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201742-61) Trump later [misrepresented](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misrepresented "Misrepresented") his high school athletic record, claiming falsely that he had been scouted by the [major leagues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball "Major League Baseball").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202471%E2%80%9372-63)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/Donald_Trump_Truth_Social_Post_on_March_13%2C_2026%E2%80%94Military_Academy.jpg/250px-Donald_Trump_Truth_Social_Post_on_March_13%2C_2026%E2%80%94Military_Academy.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Donald_Trump_Truth_Social_Post_on_March_13,_2026%E2%80%94Military_Academy.jpg)Trump and his parents at NYMA
In four out of the five years Trump attended NYMA, he made its honor roll, which required a grade average of eighty-five; in his sophomore year, he had a grade average of eighty. He was not in the highest ten percent of his class. He earned a class geometry medal for a perfect score.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHurt199378-62) Trump, who started alongside other cadets as a private, became a corporal his sophomore year and a supply sergeant in Company E the following year. As a supply sergeant, Trump ordered a cadet to be struck with a broomstick for breaking formation. During an inspection, Trump found that a cadet, Ted Levine, had not made his bed. Trump took Levine's sheets and threw them on the floor; in response, Levine threw a combat boot at Trump and hit him. Trump then grabbed Levine and attempted to throw him out of a second-floor window, according to Levine.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201741%E2%80%9343-64) In Trump's senior year, he was promoted to captain of A Company. One month into Trump's tenure, a sergeant he commanded shoved a cadet into a wall for not reacting quickly enough. Amid other [hazing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazing "Hazing") controversies at NYMA, Trump was relieved of his position and reassigned as a battalion training officer.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201744-65)
As a senior, Trump was appointed to lead a special drill team for the [Columbus Day Parade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbus_Day_Parade "Columbus Day Parade") on [Fifth Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_Avenue "Fifth Avenue").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201744-65) He became known for bringing beautiful women to the academy;[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201741-66) Trump's senior-year yearbook identified him as class "ladies' man".[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlair2000237-56) By that year, Trump had become determined that he would assume control of Fred's business, [the Fred Trump Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Trump_Organization "The Trump Organization").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlair2000238-59) He graduated from NYMA in May 1964[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201745-67) with a B average;[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBarrett201674-68) Trump's grades remained sealed after [Michael Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Cohen_\(lawyer\) "Michael Cohen \(lawyer\)"), later his personal lawyer, told his high school, his colleges, and the [College Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_Board "College Board") not to release his grades or [SAT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAT "SAT") scores.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-69) Trump had earned only a few ordinary medals, so he borrowed 12 medals from a friend for his senior-year portrait.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202468%E2%80%9369-1) At the academy's graduation ceremony the following month, Trump received a single distinction: an honorary saber for serving as a captain.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202469%E2%80%9370-70) As the [Vietnam War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam War") intensified,[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202471-60) Trump was able to defer [the draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War_draft "Vietnam War draft") by choosing to attend college.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201745-67) In the summer after graduation, Trump worked for Fred at the Swifton Village apartment complex in [Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati "Cincinnati").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201745-67)
## University
### Fordham University
After graduating from NYMA, Trump considered attending the [University of Southern California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Southern_California "University of Southern California")'s [film school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USC_School_of_Cinematic_Arts "USC School of Cinematic Arts") to study film,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201745-67)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-71) but chose to enroll at [Fordham University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fordham_University "Fordham University"), a private Jesuit [research university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_university "Research university") in [the Bronx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bronx "The Bronx"), because it was nearer to his parents' home.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlair2000239-72) His decision disappointed his father, Fred, who preferred that Trump attend the [Wharton School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wharton_School "Wharton School") of the [University of Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania "University of Pennsylvania"), an institution that his brother [Freddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Trump_Jr. "Fred Trump Jr.") had likewise rejected. Trump's sister [Maryanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryanne_Trump_Barry "Maryanne Trump Barry") privately said that she had helped get him into Fordham.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202472-73) Trump commuted from Jamaica Estates to Fordham's campus. As a freshman, Trump's wealth and military background put him at a distance from other students, as did his abstinence from smoking and drinking. He joined the school's squash team that year and sought to integrate himself into the culture.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlair2000239%E2%80%93240-74) At Fordham, he studied economics.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-75) At the school, two friends introduced him to the game of golf, which he grew to love. On warmer days, he often skipped class to play golf.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202498-76)
Trump was recruited for the school's Division III football club as a [punter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punter_\(gridiron_football\) "Punter \(gridiron football\)") but quit in about three or four weeks after he injured his ankle. He also participated in Fordham's tennis team.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBarrett201674-68) He worked on his father's [Trump Village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump_Village "Trump Village") during school breaks.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTED'Antonio201552-77) Trump did not take notes in class; he learned the material verbally from a study partner. He participated in Fordham's [Reserve Officers' Training Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserve_Officers'_Training_Corps "Reserve Officers' Training Corps") program but withdrew his [sophomore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophomore "Sophomore") year as the [Vietnam War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam War") escalated; cadets commit to being assigned as commissioned officers, assuring that they would be given a tour of duty in Vietnam. At universities, professors—wary of sending young men to war—often elevated their grades to ensure that they would pass. Trump was pressed to do well in his classes. He did not make the [dean's list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dean's_list "Dean's list") his freshman year.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202498%E2%80%9399-78)
### University of Pennsylvania
During Trump's sophomore year, he told an NYMA alumnus that he intended to [transfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_transfer "College transfer") to the Wharton School to "make better contacts for [his] future."[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202499-79) Later, his brother Freddy asked a high-school friend who worked at the University of Pennsylvania admissions office to help get Trump admitted. At that time, Trump met the grade requirements, and the school was not yet very selective.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner202499-79) Penn's prestige appealed to the Trumps.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHaberman202228-16) According to [Michael D'Antonio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_D'Antonio "Michael D'Antonio") in _[Never Enough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Never_Enough:_Donald_Trump_and_the_Pursuit_of_Success "Never Enough: Donald Trump and the Pursuit of Success")_ (2015), Fred was insistent that his son graduate from an [Ivy League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivy_League "Ivy League") institution, despite Trump's desires to forgo formal education.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTED'Antonio201568-80) Trump was not a member of any club, sports team, or fraternity at Penn, and he was not photographed for his senior-year yearbook.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBarrett201675-81) He later claimed to be a top student—"first" in his Penn Wharton School class of 333—but actually did not even make the honor roll.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201747%E2%80%9348-82) Trump told [Timothy L. O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_L._O'Brien "Timothy L. O'Brien") for _[TrumpNation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TrumpNation "TrumpNation")_ that his performance at Wharton required that he "break out of that mold".[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Brien200551-83)
As [opposition to United States involvement in the Vietnam War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opposition_to_United_States_involvement_in_the_Vietnam_War "Opposition to United States involvement in the Vietnam War") mounted on college campuses, Penn was largely distanced from activism. Though Trump personally opposed the war, he did not participate in [protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_protests_against_the_Vietnam_War "List of protests against the Vietnam War").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTED'Antonio201568%E2%80%9369-84) Trump graduated from the Wharton School in May 1968 with a [Bachelor of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") degree in economics.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-85) His graduation made him eligible for the draft after education deferments for attending Fordham University and Penn.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-Greenberg-2025-86) He visited a podiatrist who discovered that Trump had [bone spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone_spur "Bone spur") in his heels—Trump could play sports but was disqualified from the military. The finding may have been supported by a second medical opinion.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTECraigBuettner2024103-87) Two months after his medical deferment,[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-Greenberg-2025-86) in the [Vietnam War draft lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War_draft#The_1969_Draft_Lottery "Vietnam War draft"), which randomly ranked dates of birth for conscription, Trump's birthday happened to be drawn near the end of the list, receiving the high number 356 out of 366 and effectively sparing him from the mandatory draft.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_education_of_Donald_Trump#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKranishFisher201748-88)
